small_guidance:
- Sweep BLOCK_DHW over {128, 256, 512, 1024} with num_warps in {4, 8} via `triton.autotune`; current 256/8 may be suboptimal for the 16×62×62 output spatial size.
- The inner gather loads `x_val` with `BLOCK_DHW` mask per (ic,kd,kh,kw); hoist the `dhw_mask` computation and consider tiling along OH×OW only (keeping OD as a third grid axis) so loads of adjacent ow are truly contiguous and coalesce better.
- Pre-load all weights for a given OC slice into registers once outside the spatial loop (weights are tiny: OC*IC*27 = 1296 floats), avoiding re-loading inside the static_range nest.
large_guidance:
- Switch to an im2col-style implicit-GEMM: one program per (N, OC_tile, OHW_tile), accumulate as a `tl.dot` over K=IC*KD*KH*KW with BLOCK_K=32, BLOCK_M=OC(=16 padded to 32), BLOCK_N=64-128. This leverages tensor cores instead of the current outer-product accumulation and should sharply cut runtime.
- Use channels-last (NDHWC) input layout so the GEMM-K dimension (IC*kd*kh*kw) is contiguous in memory; do a one-shot permute on input (or fold into a prologue kernel) so inner loop loads coalesce on the channel axis.
- Process OD as part of the grid (pid_d) rather than flattening D*H*W, so the per-program tile lives in a single depth slice — this lets you reuse loaded input rows across kh/kw iterations and reduces redundant gathers.
